trust_decision.summary: Whether a guest-image-relative injection path stays inside the mounted guest fs is decided in _join_and_check_path_within_fs, which resolves symlinks with os.path.realpath as the unprivileged nova user, so symlinks under root-only guest dirs are not resolved before root-privileged mkdir/tee/cp write through them to the host.

landing_point.why: The summary says file injection overwrites host files; the only path-containment check for injection is this realpath line, and the existing tests at nova/tests/test_virt.py:88-103 point straight at it.

fix_sites.entry_point: POST /servers (personality, key_name, adminPass, metadata) and POST /servers/{id}/action rebuild -> libvirt/xenapi/baremetal spawn -> disk.inject_data / inject_files / inject_data_into_fs
none (rootwrap filter config allowing readlink as root; supports the api.py change)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: Only one check site; nova/rootwrap/compute.py is a supporting allowlist entry, not a second check. All callers (nova/virt/disk/api.py:239, nova/virt/disk/api.py:254, nova/virt/xenapi/vm_utils.py:1758, nova/virt/baremetal/proxy.py:477) funnel through the same helper.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: No route to dismiss: every write into the guest fs (key, net, metadata, admin password, personality files) already calls the one helper, so fixing the helper covers all of them.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Legitimate injection into normal guest paths (root/.ssh/authorized_keys append, etc/network/interfaces, etc/passwd+shadow, meta.js, nested personality paths needing mkdir -p) must keep working; symlinks inside the guest that resolve inside the guest root must still be accepted.

O6_input_shapes: '..' traversal in personality path (already handled at pinned commit)
absolute path with leading '/' (lstrip at nova/virt/disk/api.py:324)
symlink inside a guest directory that the nova user cannot traverse (the newly handled case)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a xenapi-specific helper that writes a file (e.g. hostname or agent config) into tmpdir with os.path.join and a root tee, bypassing disk.api
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: xenapi already mounts the guest itself and probes paths with plain os.path.join (nova/virt/xenapi/vm_utils.py:1719, 1731); a maintainer adding a xen-only file write there could plausibly skip the disk.api helper.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a chown/chmod or mkdir on a guest path built with os.path.join instead of the checked helper (e.g. on the authorized_keys file itself)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the key path is already re-joined unchecked at nova/virt/disk/api.py:355 before being checked inside _inject_file_into_fs; adding a direct chmod 600 on it would be a natural hardening tweak.

O9_family: path traversal / symlink following out of a mounted guest filesystem into host files (privileged write)

O10_build.toolchain: pip/virtualenv with 2012-era Essex requirements (eventlet, sqlalchemy 0.7, Cheetah, boto, etc.); old pins likely need a frozen mirror
O10_build.project_tests: nova/tests/test_virt.py:88-103 (TestVirtDisk path checks), nova/tests/test_xenapi.py spawn-with-injection tests using fake_utils execute repliers

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add more '..'/os.path.normpath checks or os.path.islink rejection in the helper, still running as the nova user, which cannot see the symlink in a root-only guest directory.

out_of_scope_notes: TOCTOU between the resolve and the later root mkdir/tee (nova/virt/disk/api.py:326-336) exists in principle but the guest is not running during injection; not pursued.
unverified: O1 counts the OpenStack API create and rebuild routes; EC2 RunInstances (nova/api/ec2/cloud.py:1304) reaches key injection too but its exact injection fields were not traced.

Behavioural testability: reproducing the flaw needs a symlink the test user cannot resolve but root can; offline non-root tests can only stub utils.execute (as the published tests do), so a hidden test may pin the implementation rather than the behaviour.
